character_facts: The four surviving whore-priestesses of Shabda-Oud are acting together in a conspiracy or raid.
At least one priestess is treated as a commanding maternal authority, called 'Mother.'
They are cybernetically integrated or shown within a highly biomechanical apparatus.
They are cautious and prepare specifically against psychic or mental interrogation.
characters_present: The four surviving whore-priestesses of Shabda-Oud
Servitor or attendant figures addressing one of them as 'Mother'
continuity_links: This page opens with a transition during transport to Kgen-Kgen and sets up a prison-related infiltration or raid.
The page establishes the priestesses' covert action as a parallel plot underway before arrival.
dialogue_meaning: The priestesses issue covert operational commands for an imminent raid.
They expect hostile mental scanning and take measures to prevent their minds or spirits from being read.
Their attendants or systems acknowledge each command as completed and address their leader as 'Mother.'
locations: A spacecraft heading toward the prison satellite Kgen-Kgen
The Empire's prison satellite Kgen-Kgen (mentioned, not directly shown in detail)
lore_facts: Kgen-Kgen is an abominable titanium satellite and is described as the Empire's most dreaded prison.
An octocyborg can contain occupants and serve as a command environment.
The whore-priestesses of Shabda-Oud have only four survivors at this point.
A device, vessel, or system called the Kantylopter can be awakened or activated.
An invisibility shield exists in this setting.
Mental probes are a known threat in this universe.
'Emptying' one's spirits is presented as a defense against mental probing.
plot_events: A vessel is en route to the Empire's dreaded prison satellite, Kgen-Kgen.
An act of treachery or a covert plan begins during the journey.
Inside an octocyborg, the four surviving whore-priestesses of Shabda-Oud plan a raid.
They order the Kantylopter to be awakened.
They order an invisibility shield to be activated.
They order their spirits to be emptied because mental probes are expected.
Subordinate beings confirm that the Kantylopter is awake, the shield is active, and the spirits are emptied.
uncertainties: Some labels and names are stylized and may be slightly misread; 'Kantylopter' and 'Kgen-Kgen' are read from small text.
The exact nature of the small angular object near the larger ship is unclear from this page alone.
It is unclear whether the speaker called 'Mother' is one of the four priestesses or a separate central entity within the octocyborg.
visual_summary: A large organic-looking spacecraft travels through space toward a prison satellite while a smaller angular craft or object floats nearby. Captions explain that treachery is underway during the journey to the Empire's feared prison, Kgen-Kgen. Inside a biomechanical chamber, four cybernetic women identified as the surviving whore-priestesses of Shabda-Oud command the awakening of the Kantylopter, the activation of an invisibility shield, and the emptying of their spirits to avoid mental probing. Servitor-like figures report each command completed to 'Mother.'
